1] Heard.
 2] This criminal revision has been f under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C. against the order dated 11.01.2021, passed in Criminal Case No.2551 of 2021 under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 34 & 120-B of IPC, which was registered at Crime No.389 of 2020, Police Station - Annapurna, Indore.
3] Vide the aforesaid order dated 11.01.2021, the learned J.M.F.C. has allowed the application filed by the respondent Nos.1 and 2 under Section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. claiming default bail as the charge-sheet was not filed within 60 days' time.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31833 CRR 905-2021 4] Counsel for the respondents,
at the outset, have drawn the attention of this Court that so far as the respondent Nos.3 and 4 are concerned, their application under Section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. was rejected by the trial Court and it was challenged by them before the District Revisional Court in Criminal Revision No.253 of 2020,
which was decided on 07.01.2020, in favour of respondent No.3 Nitin and respondent No.4 Sachin,
and default bail was granted to them by the Revisional Court itself, however, 5] The aforesaid order The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Gaurav on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78354907/
1 passed in Criminal Revision No.253 of 2020 has not been challenged by the State, and the present criminal revision has been preferred only in respect of the order of J.M.F.C. dated 11.01.2021,
whereby the default bail was allowed in respect of respondent No.1- Gaurav and respondent No.2 Manoj.

6] Counsel have also submitted that the names of respondent Nos.3 and 4 have already been directed to be deleted by the order passed by this court on 21.09.2024, and in such circumstances,
the present revision itself is not maintainable as the State has already accepted the order passed by the Revisional Court arising out of the same issue of default bail.

It is also submitted that even otherwise, the State has directly come before this Court in its revisional jurisdiction without first applying for the same before the District Court, and thus, the State has also deprived the respondents of a remedy available to the them under law, in case, if the revision is allowed by the District Court.

On due consideration of submissions, perusal of the documents filed on record and also taking note of the order passed by the Revisional Court on 07.01.2020, in Cr.R. No.253 of 2020, this Court is of the considered opinion that the State cannot be allowed to adopt a policy of pick and choose, and while allowing the respondent Nos.3 and 4 to be released on default bail, the State cannot contend that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 should not be given the same benefit, especially when the default bail order itself is of 11.01.2021, whereas, the order passed in Criminal Revision No.253/2020 was passed on 07.01.2020.
8] Accordingly, present criminal revision is hereby dismissed.
9 ] The learned Judge of the trial Court is requested to proceed further, in accordance with law.
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Pankaj The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Gaurav on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78354907/
